raw_case_text:
Patient 1 was a previously healthy, 26-year-old Peruvian man who was evaluated in July 1985 for a 3-month history of periorbital pain, headaches, and periodic generalized tonic-clonic seizures. The initial neurologic examination was nonfocal, but subsequent computerized tomography scan showed a 5x5-cm enhancing mass in the left frontoparietal region associated with midline shift.
At the time of surgical biopsy, frozen section histology raised the possibility of a high-grade astrocytoma or lymphoma, prompting resection of a 3x3-cm well-circumscribed left frontal lobe mass. Final examination of pathologic specimens showed granulomas with multinucleated giant cells (Figure 1). Bacterial, fungal, and acid-fast bacilli stains were negative. Based on these pathologic findings and concern that the patient may have had tuberculosis, treatment with isoniazid, rifampin, and ethambutol was begun. Serologic tests for Histoplasma capsulatum, Blastomyces dermatidis, Coccidioides immitis, and Paracoccidioides brasiliensis were negative. Toxoplasma gondii serologic titers were weakly positive at 1:64.
On postoperative day 39, fungal tissue cultures became positive for a Brucella spp., preliminarily identified as B. melitensis. The patient's antimicrobial treatment was changed to tetracycline and rifampin and was continued for 2 months. An initial serologic titer for Brucella was positive at 1:160 by tube agglutination assay. A follow-up serologic titer obtained in January 1986 was negative (<1:20).
Three months before his initial evaluation, the patient had immigrated to the United States from Lima, Peru. His diet included regular consumption of unpasteurized cow or goat cheese (queso fresco) and occasional consumption of raw shellfish (ceviche). He denied eating other raw or significantly undercooked meat. He had frequently swum in the Pacific Ocean from December through March but recalled no direct contact with marine mammals.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 26-year-old Peruvian male presented with a 3-month history of periorbital pain, headaches, and periodic generalized tonic-clonic seizures.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient was previously healthy until 3 months prior to presentation in July 1985, when he developed progressive periorbital pain, headaches, and periodic generalized tonic-clonic seizures.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy. Epidemiological/dietary history: emigrated from Lima, Peru to the United States 3 months prior to presentation; regular consumption of unpasteurized cow or goat cheese (queso fresco) and occasional consumption of raw shellfish (ceviche); denied eating other raw or undercooked meat; swam frequently in the Pacific Ocean (December to March) with no marine mammal contact.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports periorbital pain, headaches, and periodic seizures. Denies other systemic symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: Initial neurologic examination was nonfocal. General physical examination was otherwise unremarkable.
objective.advanced_workup: Contrast-enhanced head CT demonstrated a 5 x 5 cm enhancing mass in the left frontoparietal region associated with midline shift. Resection of a 3 x 3 cm well-circumscribed left frontal lobe mass was performed; frozen section suggested high-grade astrocytoma or lymphoma, but final histopathology showed granulomas with multinucleated giant cells; bacterial, fungal, and acid-fast bacilli stains were negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmation: On postoperative day 39, tissue fungal cultures grew Brucella spp., preliminarily identified as Brucella melitensis, confirming neurobrucellosis presenting as a solitary cerebral brucelloma. Initial serum tube agglutination titer for Brucella was positive at 1:160. Differential diagnoses ruled out: Brain neoplasm (high-grade astrocytoma and lymphoma) excluded by final histopathology; tuberculosis excluded by negative acid-fast bacilli stains; serologic testing for endemic fungi (Histoplasma capsulatum, Blastomyces dermatitidis, Coccidioides immitis, Paracoccidioides brasiliensis) was negative; Toxoplasma gondii titer was weakly positive at 1:64 (non-diagnostic). Management and Outcome: Initially treated empirically for tuberculosis with isoniazid, rifampin, and ethambutol. Following microbiological confirmation, therapy was switched to oral tetracycline and rifampin for 2 months. Follow-up Brucella serology obtained in January 1986 turned negative (<1:20), indicating full clinical and serologic resolution.
